'''Liberman's lemma''' is a theorem used in studying [[intrinsic metric|intrinsic geometry]] of [[convex surface]].
It is named after [[Joseph Liberman]].

==Formulation==

If <math>\gamma</math> is a unit-speed minimizing [[geodesic]] on the surface of a [[convex body]] ''K'' in [[Euclidean space]] then for any point ''p''&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;''K'', the function

: <math>t\mapsto\operatorname{dist}^2\circ\gamma(t)-t^2 </math>

is concave.

==References==
*Либерман, И. М. «Геодезические линии на выпуклых поверхностях». ДАН СССР. 32.2. (1941), 310—313.
